summary:
Radar, 20 Oct 2026. The strongest lane is still gray-market topics framed as "what's confirmed?", and this week it has fresh news behind it. CBS News reported on 13 Oct that the FDA has received two death reports linked to products sold as "retatrutide". Futurism picked this up on 17 Oct and NL Times reported black-market retatrutide spreading in the Netherlands on 19 Oct. Separately, compounded tirzepatide is back in the news: USA Today and LA Times stories from 19 Oct cover the Apothecary Pharma Class II recall and the Chinese ingredient plants with mold problems. These are the best fits for this week's 2 Lane B long-forms.

One correction: the "Lilly sues six retatrutide sellers" item in today's feed is a Stocktwits repost of news from 12 Aug 2026. It is not new, so date it that way if you use it.

Orforglipron's ACHIEVE-4 trial (1 Oct, Lilly) is a real randomized head-to-head against insulin glargine in people with type 2 diabetes at higher heart risk. That suits the head-to-head Short format, which also works on Instagram.

For Lane A search-question long-forms, three topics are timed well:
- "sick on your GLP-1, or a bug?", with cold and flu season starting and a Yahoo story from 19 Oct
- "why am I not losing weight on tirzepatide/semaglutide?"
- "what happens when you stop?", refreshed by a 19 Oct study naming copay cost as a reason people stop

Two other items are dated. The Zepbound KwikPen was approved in January 2026, and the Wegovy subscription started 31 Mar 2026, so neither is new.

Early-stage science hooks: a semaglutide handgrip-strength meta-analysis (Diabetes Obes Metab, 19 Oct; the abstract couldn't be loaded, so verify it before scripting), a low-dose semaglutide heart study in rats and minipigs (Cedars-Sinai, 13 Oct; animal data only), and a meta-analysis of randomized trials on PCOS pregnancy rates.

Rejected: a "low-dose tirzepatide strategy" item, because it invites dosing and self-titration content.

candidates.topic: Retatrutide online: what the FDA and Lilly have actually confirmed (Oct 2026). FDA death reports linked to products sold as 'retatrutide' (CBS News investigation, 13 Oct 2026), Lilly's lawsuits (12 Aug 2026) and spread of the black market to Europe
candidates.angle:
Lane B long-form plus a 13:00 lead Short, in the calm 'What's Actually Confirmed?' frame. Facts to cover:
- Retatrutide is not approved by any regulator as of Oct 2026.
- The FDA says it cannot legally be compounded.
- CBS reported 2 death reports to the FDA, one in July and one in September. They are unverified, and it's unknown what the products actually contained.
- Lilly says 'what is being sold on the black market is not a medicine' (12 Aug 2026).
Credit and date every line. Never name a seller (the lawsuit defendants included). Close by pointing viewers to a prescriber about approved options or clinical trials. No scare faces.
candidates.why_now: The CBS death-report story (13 Oct) is now spreading: Futurism (17 Oct), NL Times on the Netherlands (19 Oct), Gizmodo, NewsNation. Dozens of SEO pages are targeting 'retatrutide approval status'. Our best Short lane (median 103.5) has never been tested as a long-form, and the growth playbook calls for 2 Lane B long-forms this week.

evidence.signal: Investigation: bootleg weight-loss drug linked to 2 recent deaths reported to the FDA
Black market retatrutide linked to multiple deaths; FDA reports
Details: a 41-year-old with cardiac arrest (July report) and a 49-year-old with dehydration, malnutrition and cardiac arrest (September); unverified
Lilly's 6 lawsuits and the CMO quote; seized samples ranged from zero dose to overdose, some contained insulin
Illegal retatrutide on the rise in the Netherlands

candidates.topic: Compounded tirzepatide recall: what the FDA confirmed about 22 Apothecary Pharma vials (Class II, 10 Oct 2026), plus the FDA's findings at Chinese ingredient plants (LA Times, 19 Oct)
candidates.angle:
Lane B long-form titled 'Compounded Tirzepatide Recall: What the FDA Confirmed (Oct 2026)'. Cover only what the FDA notices and inspection reports say:
- the reason was 'lack of assurance of sterility'
- the specific lots recalled
- the December 2025 warning letter to the same pharmacy
- the import alert on the ingredient plants
Explain the difference between FDA-approved pens and compounded vials, and say what to ask your pharmacist or prescriber. Don't tell anyone to stop or switch on their own. No #Mounjaro or #Zepbound hashtags.
candidates.why_now: USA Today's recall story (19 Oct) has been syndicated to Yahoo and AOL. LA Times covered the plant findings the same day. Medical Daily reported FDA inspection observations at a Houston recall pharmacy (19 Oct). People searching for this want a calm explainer. Our compounded Short got 91 views.

evidence.signal: 22 vials of compounded tirzepatide recalled nationwide; voluntary recall started 24 Sep, upgraded to Class II on 10 Oct 2026
Black mold and bugs found at Chinese plants making GLP-1 compounding ingredients
Houston pharmacy behind recalled tirzepatide vials drew 14 FDA inspection observations

candidates.topic: Orforglipron (Foundayo) versus insulin glargine: heart attacks, strokes and deaths in ACHIEVE-4 (2,749 adults with type 2 diabetes at higher heart risk, announced by Lilly 1 Oct 2026)
candidates.angle:
Two-drug head-to-head Short with both drugs named, which is our cross-platform winner. This was a real randomized comparison. Facts to give:
- MACE-4 risk 16% lower (relative; the main goal was non-inferiority)
- A1C down 1.6 points versus 1.0
- weight down 8.8% versus up 1.7% at 52 weeks
Call the death findings 'pre-planned secondary analyses', with absolute rates beside them. Fold in the EU status: CHMP positive opinion, Commission decision pending. Don't make a standalone 'approved yet?' piece.
candidates.why_now: Clinical Trial Vanguard (19 Oct) argues the result raises the bar for every oral GLP-1 behind it. The EU recommendation came this week. Orforglipron Shorts underperformed in the past, so lean on the named head-to-head format here.

evidence.signal: ACHIEVE-4: 16% lower MACE-4, 23% lower MACE-3 versus insulin glargine; 53% lower cardiovascular death in pre-planned analyses
Noninferior to insulin glargine for cardiovascular outcomes in type 2 diabetes
Cardiovascular safety, A1C and weight data

candidates.topic: Sick on tirzepatide or semaglutide this cold and flu season: is it a side effect or a bug? Staying hydrated and when to call your prescriber
candidates.angle:
Lane A long-form titled 'Feeling Sick on Tirzepatide? Side Effect or Stomach Bug' (Life on GLP-1 series). Cover:
- the label's common stomach side effects, and how they tend to ease over time
- why low intake can cause tiredness and headaches
- hydration, with 'unless you've been told to limit fluids'
- the label warning about dehydration and kidney problems, and when to call your prescriber
No dose-skipping or dosing advice: 'ask your prescriber what to do'.
candidates.predicted_peak: 2–6 weeks, as the flu season builds
candidates.why_now: Yahoo Creators ran 'Feeling awful on your GLP-1? The drug may not be what's making you miserable' on 19 Oct. Flu and norovirus season is starting in the US, UK, Canada and Australia. Side-effect searches are steady and high, and our stomach side-effects Short won on both platforms.

evidence.signal: Feeling awful on your GLP-1? The drug may not be the cause
Stomach symptom events and motility changes with GLP-1 receptor agonists

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide versus semaglutide: who stopped more often because of side effects? (SURMOUNT-5, adults with obesity without diabetes, 72 weeks)
candidates.angle: Two-drug body-effect head-to-head Short for the 13:00 slot. Name the drug next to each discontinuation rate. Include the 'don't switch or stop on your own' line. Use SURMOUNT-5 in at most 1 Short this week.
candidates.why_now: Tracked in 11 snapshots with steady momentum. 'Tirzepatide vs semaglutide' searches are always on, and this is the playbook's top double-down idea.

evidence.signal: Seen 11 times at momentum 78–80; the stomach side-effects Short got 90 views and 103 Instagram reach

candidates.topic: Why am I not losing weight on tirzepatide or semaglutide? The spread of responses in STEP and SURMOUNT
candidates.angle:
Lane A long-form titled 'Not Losing Weight on Tirzepatide? What the Trials Show'. Cover:
- how results spread across people in the trials
- the early plateau
- the habits that matter: protein, strength training (start gently), sleep
- what to ask your prescriber
Say 'smaller responders', not 'slower'. No dose changes.
keywords: why am I not losing weight on Ozempic
candidates.why_now: GoodRx ran 'Why am I not losing weight on Ozempic?' on 17 Oct. A UK real-world study of over 1 million self-paying adults (DOM, 14 Oct) adds a new data hook. Tracked in 6 snapshots.

evidence.signal: Why am I not losing weight on Ozempic? 5 reasons
Real-world weight outcomes in over 1 million self-paying UK adults on tirzepatide

candidates.topic: What happens when you stop tirzepatide or semaglutide? SURMOUNT-4 and STEP 1 extension regain data, plus a new study naming copay cost as a reason people stop
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form titled 'What Happens When You Stop Semaglutide or Tirzepatide?'. Explain what the trials showed. Frame it as 'decide with your prescriber', never as stopping advice. Cover the habits that helped people keep results: protein, strength training, activity.
keywords: what happens when you stop Mounjaro
candidates.why_now: VPM (19 Oct) reports a study that points to copay price as a reason people stop. Tracked in 6 snapshots. This is one of the playbook's suggested Lane A titles.

Weight regain after switching tirzepatide to placebo versus continuing it

candidates.topic: Does semaglutide make you weaker? A new meta-analysis of handgrip strength (Diabetes Obes Metab, 19 Oct 2026), alongside the SEMALEAN study's +4.5 kg grip result
candidates.angle: Muscle outcome question Short for the 08:00 slot: 'Semaglutide: does it weaken your grip?'. Answer from the meta-analysis and the SEMALEAN data. Pair it with protein (check first if you have kidney disease) and starting strength training gently. The abstract couldn't be loaded, so the fact-checker must confirm the pooled result before scripting.
candidates.why_now: Published 19 Oct and not yet in the news. Muscle questions are a proven format for us (99 and 130 views), and this adds a fact we haven't published.

evidence.signal: Changes in muscle strength after semaglutide: systematic review and meta-analysis of handgrip strength
Handgrip +4.5 kg at 12 months; sarcopenic obesity fell from 49% to 33%

candidates.angle: Lane A explainer built only on manufacturers' own published prices, with dates. Explain that insurance coverage varies. Never promote a telehealth company, a compounded product or a no-prescription source. Include 'don't switch on your own'.

Wegovy subscription program details (started Mar 2026)

candidates.angle: UK-focused Short or long-form segment: what the study found about who stayed on treatment, who changed, and weight outcomes. Phrase every finding as 'linked to'. Include 'don't switch or stop on your own'.

candidates.topic: Can semaglutide protect the heart even without weight loss? Low-dose semaglutide reduced heart stiffness in rats and minipigs with obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (European Heart Journal, Cedars-Sinai, 13 Oct 2026)
candidates.angle: Mechanism Short in the 'how GLP-1 works' pillar. Label it clearly as an animal study. Contrast it with the human SUMMIT and STEP-HFpEF trials and ESC 2026's first heart-failure guideline recommendation for GLP-1-based therapy. No low-dose suggestion: that would be dosing bait.
candidates.why_now: DI Cardiology picked it up on 19 Oct and the press release is spreading.

evidence.signal: Low-dose semaglutide reduced heart stiffness without significant weight loss, in animals
